courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now we had a look at all the core building blocks to styling in Ionic apps,
by the way no matter if your building an Ionic Angular or just Ionic vanilla app. Now feel free to of
course continue exploring the docs to learn about all the different properties you can set and so on,
one thing I want to point you at is that in the component documentation you'll also find for each component,
let's say for the button,, you will not only find an explanation on how to use it and which properties
and attributes you can set but if you scroll down to the bottom, you'll also find any settable CSS
properties for that specific component
if there are any and how would you use these components
now, that is also important to learn.
You see that for a button, you can set the background, background activated, box shadow, border width
and so on.
So what can you do with that?
You can set that, of course not by going to variables and adding it to root because if you start adding
--ion-background here which is a variable that is mentioned here for buttons, then this will
not have the effect you want
or by the way, it's just named background and this will even less have the effect you want.
Instead what you do is simply you set up your own variables for the specific selector,
so in the example of the button, for ion-button and that's also important, you select Ionic components
just like normal HTML elements
if you want to select them by tag,
so this is absolutely supported.
And now for ion-button, you could set up anything, you could set the color to white to set a white text
color but here you can now also use these special variables,
so here you could now set background to blue and then automatically every button would have a blue background
if you haven't assigned a specific color. So if you as for example on your auth page, if you are styling
a button with color primary, it will still have that primary color as you can tell
but if you would remove that, we're talking about the default styling that would normally be a grey-ish
look and
now if you remove that and you got that blue look or the blue color set up, then you got a blue color
out of the box.
So that is what this would allow you to do and you do assign these component specific variables by
using the components selector and then applying the variable or setting the variable you want to set.
Here I'm doing this in the variables.scss file and therefore, this will have an effect application wide
but you could even do that of course in a component.sass file to scope it to that component.
So if we're talking about the offer item again, here I could also target my ion-text and set up some
specific styles for that and then only ion-text inside of offer item would be affected,
so that would not be having an effect application wide. Hence it's important to also keep in mind that
where you set this up plays an important role and that in general, you can also set component specific
properties. For the color,
this might be less necessary because often you want to use your main theme but maybe you want to change
the way the shadow looks on all buttons because by default here on Android, we have a slight drop shadow,
maybe you're not happy with that and you want to use a different one,
well then you can simply add ion-button and then set shadow which is simply this box shadow,
this variable, so box-shadow and then we could set this to let's say 2px 2px 20px
and then this shadow style overall.
So now this would be a default value you would assign to the box shadow property,
here I'm assigning it to the box shadow variable which as we learned is supported by Ionic and is picked
up by the button and therefore now, we have a larger shadow on this button as you can tell.
So this is also what you can do, you have these component specific properties or variables you can
set and you can not just use component selectors to style anything even outside of variables, of course
you can still apply normal CSS rules but you can also use these CSS variables to set application
wide or component wide styles for a specific Ionic component.
